Complements\nthe lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference, which covers the kernel-level\nblockers; this file covers patterns where the Lean code *compiles and the\ntrick is at the level of what the statement says or what the definitions\nbake in*.\n\nEvery pattern here is **castle-in-the-air in spirit**: a theorem named after a\npaper result that doesn't actually prove it. The named offenders below all\ncross-reference a concrete issue or PR so reviewers can see a real example.\n\n## Why this matters\n\nKernel checks are necessary but not sufficient. A theorem can:\n\n- Be marked `\\leanok` in the blueprint,\n- Have a sorry-free proof body,\n- Have a clean axiom closure (`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound` only),\n\nand still prove **nothing that the paper actually claims**, if the proof\nobligation has been displaced into a hypothesis, a definition, or a sentinel\nbranch. The patterns below are the displacement mechanisms we've seen in this\ncodebase.\n\n## Catalogue\n\n- [A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis](#a1--conclusion-shaped-hypothesis)\n- [A2 — Definitional sleight-of-hand](#a2--definitional-sleight-of-hand)\n- [A3 — Zero-fallback branches hiding preconditions](#a3--zero-fallback-branches-hiding-preconditions)\n- [A4 — Trivial default witnesses for existentials](#a4--trivial-default-witnesses-for-existentials)\n- [A5 — Castle-in-the-air / bypassing Mathlib](#a5--castle-in-the-air--bypassing-mathlib)\n- [A6 — External `*Statement` smuggles](#a6--external-statement-smuggles)\n\n---\n\n## A1 — Conclusion-shaped hypothesis\n\n**Smell.** The theorem takes a hypothesis whose type is the theorem's own\nconclusion (or an `∃`/function that produces the conclusion). The proof body\nis a trivial `rcases`/`exact`/`.trans`/`simpa using h` and does no\nmathematical work. A variant wraps the hypothesis in a named bundle\n(`*BridgePackage`, `*Statement`); see issues [#449], [#451], [#477] for the\ncatalogue, and [#493] for the inline-existential mutation triggered by\nPR [#491].\n\n### Why it's bad\n\nThe theorem's named mathematical content is never derived from prior lemmas;\nthe caller (who supplies the hypothesis) has to discharge it. In practice the\ncaller then has the same problem, pushing the obligation further up the\nstack. The theorem is true under a vacuous hypothesis and the `\\leanok` tag\nmisrepresents the actual state of the proof.\n\n### How to spot it\n\n- The hypothesis type contains, up to `∃` / `∧` / a coercion, the theorem's\n  conclusion.\n- The proof body is one of:\n  - `rcases h with ⟨...⟩; exact ⟨...⟩`\n  - `exact h.fieldName` / `exact h.a.trans h.b`\n  - `by simpa using h.fieldName`\n- The hypothesis is a bundle named `*BridgePackage`, `*Witness`, `*Package`,\n  `*Output`, with a field whose type matches the conclusion structure.\n- Consumers of the bundle are trivial (field projection + return).\n\n### Concrete example\n\nHistorical example (before the MainInductionStep cleanup):\n\n```lean\ntheorem mainInduction\n    (params : Parameters) [FieldModel params.q]\n    (strategy : SymStrat params ι)\n    (eps delta gamma : Error) (k : ℕ)\n    (hbridge : MainInductionBridgePackage params strategy eps delta gamma k) :\n    ∃ G : Measurement (Polynomial params) ι,\n      ConsRel strategy.state ...\n        (mainInductionError params k eps delta gamma) := by\n  rcases hbridge.witness with ⟨error, G, hG, herror⟩\n  refine ⟨G, ?_⟩\n  exact ⟨le_trans hG.offDiagonalBound herror⟩\n```\n\nHere `MainInductionBridgePackage.witness` has type\n`∃ error, ∃ G, ConsRel ... error ∧ error ≤ mainInductionError ...` — literally\nthe conclusion. The code has since been refactored to remove both this\nspecific MainInductionStep bridge and the interim theorem alias that exposed\nthe same witness shape under the paper theorem's name, but the snippet remains\nthe archetypal example of the anti-pattern.\n\nPR [#491] proposed to delete the `*BridgePackage` by **inlining** the bundle's\nfields as explicit hypotheses. That only scatters the same pattern across\nindividual signatures without producing any proof — it's strictly worse\nbecause the named bundle at least shows up in one tracker. Do not accept PRs\nthat discharge an ungrounded bridge by flattening it into conclusion-shaped\nexistential hypotheses, or by reintroducing the same shape under a theorem name\nthat suggests the paper result has been proved.\n\n### How to fix it\n\nPrefer **proving a real intermediate lemma** — one that the paper also uses\n— and stating its signature with the paper's hypotheses (not the theorem's\nconclusion). Then use it inside the larger theorem. For Section 5, for\\nexample, prefer orthogonalization lemma, truncation function, rounding to\\nprojectors, rank reduction, and completing to measurement.\\n\\n## Reference Notation And Terminology\\n\\nThe notation and terminology of the original reference are the default for\\nreader-facing mathematical text.  A reader should be able to compare a Lean\\ndocstring, blueprint paragraph, issue, or PR description with the cited source\\nwithout first learning a private vocabulary used by the formalization.\\n\\nWhen Lean must use a different name or representation, define the deviation in a\\nlocation which future readers can find from the affected statement.  Use the\\nfirst applicable location in the following order:\\n\\n1. the declaration docstring of the public object whose name or representation\\n   differs from the paper;\\n2. the module docstring of the defining Lean file, when the deviation concerns a\\n   family of declarations in that file;\\n3. the relevant blueprint paragraph, when the notation appears only in the\\n   blueprint;\\n4. a report under `docs/reports/` or `docs/paper-gaps/`, when the deviation is a\\n   larger discrepancy between the paper, blueprint, and Lean.\\n\\nThe explanation should say:\\n\\n- the notation or term used in the paper;\\n- the Lean object or name which represents it;\\n- the mathematical reason for the difference, if there is one;\\n- the scope in which the replacement should be used.\\n\\nA PR description may mention the deviation, but it should not be the only place\\nwhere future readers can learn it.\\n\\nFormalization-only auxiliary lemmas should be introduced as such.  Their prose\\nshould name the nearby paper equation, theorem, or construction they support,\\nrather than presenting the auxiliary name as paper terminology.\\n\\n## Naming Norm\\n\\nNames and prose should describe the mathematical object, hypothesis, or\\nconclusion. They should not encode the history of how the formalization was\\nassembled.\\n\\nAvoid presenting words such as `pipeline`, `wrapper`, `package`, `raw`,\\n`oneShot`, or `liveBlock` as mathematical terminology unless the cited source\\nuses them with that meaning. Likewise, avoid implementation-local substitutes\\nsuch as `projectivization` or `spectral truncation` when the paper gives a\\nclearer phrase.\\n\\nThis is a general rule for the repository, not only a rule for file splits.\\nModule names, namespace names, public declarations, theorem fields, docstrings,\\nblueprint-facing names, issue titles, and spec documents should name the\\nmathematical layer under discussion, not the local workflow step, paper line\\nnumber, or implementation history.\\n\\n### Concrete examples\\n\\nThe table below illustrates the naming norm with examples patterned on the\\ncodebase and on names seen during review.  Some entries are existing names;\\nothers are proposed names for future refactors.  The \\\"avoid\\\" column lists\\nprocess-shaped names that encode the history of how the formalization was\\nassembled; the \\\"prefer\\\" column lists mathematical names that a reader of the\\npaper |\\n|:----------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|\\n| `Line130` declarations\\nexposed by the split should be reviewed under the same standard.\\n\\n### Shared helpers\\n\\nWhen the same (or nearly the same) helper declaration appears in two or\\nmore chapter-local leaves, the copies should be consolidated into a single\\nshared helper in an appropriate common module.  This avoids duplication and\\nensures that fixes, generalizations, or upstream replacements apply to all\\ncall sites at once. Root imports\\nflow: `MIPStarRE.lean` → `Quantum` + `LDT` → all submodules.\\n\\n## Quick Start — Build and Check Commands\\n\\nRun commands from the repository root unless noted otherwise.\\n\\n### First-time setup\\n\\n```bash\\nlake exe cache get\\nlake build\\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh\\nscripts/install_git_hooks.sh --check\\n```\\n\\nRun the hook check in every fresh worktree before preparing a PR. Section 6: main induction wrapper\\n\\nDo not start from the final theorem and guess intermediate facts.\\n\\n## Faithful Formalization Policy\\n\\nA declaration is a formalization of a paper theorem only when its public Lean\\nstatement matches the cited paper statement, up to faithful formal encoding.\\nChanging a Lean theorem away from the corresponding statement in\\n`references/ldt-paper/` is strongly discouraged and should occur only when a\\nfaithful formal encoding or a documented mathematical necessity requires it.\\nThis applies to every declaration advertised as a formalization of a paper\\nresult, not only to theorems currently undergoing repair.  The check is on the\\nhypotheses as well as the conclusion.  A theorem whose\\nconclusion has the right shape but whose assumptions include an extra\\nload-bearing bridge input or hypotheses bundle is a conditional theorem, not\\nthe paper theorem.\\nThe project goal is to eliminate such conditional bridges, not to normalize\\nthem as permanent infrastructure.\\n\\nIf the only available Lean theorem has extra assumptions, the blueprint must\\nnot mark the source-labelled paper entry as matched by that theorem.  Either\\nleave the source-labelled entry without `\\\\leanok`, or state the restricted or\\nconditional result as a separate Lean-only blueprint entry whose hypotheses are\\ndisplayed explicitly.  A scope-restricted theorem may be marked `\\\\leanok` only\\nagainst a blueprint statement that explicitly states the restriction; it must\\nnot be presented as the unrestricted source theorem.\\n\\nWhen a stricter-hypothesis Lean theorem is the only available version near a\\nsource theorem, the discrepancy must have a paper-gap note or tracking issue.\\nThe note should identify the missing hypothesis, explain why it is not part of\\nthe cited statement, and state the plan for eliminating the restriction,\\nderiving it internally, or moving the result out of the source-labelled route.\\n\\nThis rule applies especially to declarations named after paper labels such as\\n`mainFormal`, `selfImprovement`, `mainInduction`, or other theorem names linked\\nfrom the blueprint by `\\\\lean{...}` and `\\\\leanok`.\\n\\nBefore editing any theorem tagged with a paper label (`thm:*`, `lem:*`,\\n`prop:*`):\\n\\n1. Do not add bridge inputs, residual packages, repair hypotheses, producer\\n   assumptions, generic hypotheses or assumptions bundles, or arbitrary\\n   implication hypotheses to the paper theorem.\\n4. If a missing intermediate fact is needed, first state that fact as a named\\n   lemma or theorem to be proved from the paper hypotheses.\\n5. Do not add a conditional helper merely to keep a file compiling.  A\\n   conditional helper may remain temporarily only when the proof content it\\n   preserves is mathematically useful, the source-faithful theorem remains\\n   visible, and the helper has a paper-gap note, a named construction theorem\\n   or proof-obligation target, and an explicit discharge or deletion plan.  Its\\n   name must show that it is conditional without making the assumption look like\\n   an acceptable source hypothesis, for example\\n   `mainFormal_ofInternalObligations`, `selfImprovementFromObligations`, or a\\n   name ending in `_ofObligations`.\\n6. A theorem\\nwith an extra hypothesis such as\\n`hbaseBridge : ... → MainFormalRepairedBridgeHypotheses ...` is temporary\\nscaffolding at best; it must not be the declaration advertised as\\n`thm:main-formal`.  The corresponding paper-aligned version should remain\\nvisible, even if its proof is temporarily unfinished during repair.\\n\\nEvery agent changing a paper-labelled theorem must finish with a statement\\nintegrity audit:\\n\\n- paper assumptions;\\n- Lean assumptions;\\n- paper conclusion;\\n- Lean conclusion;\\n- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened\\n  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.\\n\\n### Paper-realignment mode\\n\\nWhen a theorem, definition, or hypothesis field has already drifted away from\\n`references/ldt-paper/`, a repair PR may temporarily reintroduce `sorry` in\\norder to restore the source-faithful statement.  In this mode, statement\\nfaithfulness is the first invariant: keeping a divergent proof intact merely to\\navoid `sorry` preserves a theorem that the paper does not state.\\n\\nPaper-realignment mode is narrow.  It applies only to edits whose purpose is to\\nremove wrong hypotheses, delete divergent fields, restore a paper theorem\\nstatement, or replace a conditional theorem by a paper-facing statement plus a\\nnamed proof obligation. A\\nname such as `Bridge`, `Residual`, `Repair`, `Package`, `Input`, or `Producer`\\nis not by itself a mathematical source citation.\\n\\n### Unfaithful dependency markers\\n\\nA theorem or lemma is **unfaithful** when its proof relies on a hypothesis,\\nhelper, bridge, residual, repair input, or conditional theorem that is known not\\nto follow from the cited paper statement.  This includes the case where the\\npublic theorem statement is source-shaped but the proof calls a conditional\\nhelper whose load-bearing hypothesis is not yet derived from the paper\\nhypotheses.\\n\\nSuch a declaration must carry a docstring section beginning with\\n`**Unfaithful:**`.  The marker must name the load-bearing deviation, cite the\\npaper-gap note or issue that documents it, and state the planned discharge.  A\\nminimal form is:\\n\\n```text\\n**Unfaithful:** This proof currently relies on `<hypothesis or helper>`,\\nwhich is not derived from `<paper label or line range>`. Elimination: prove\\n`<construction theorem>` from the paper hypotheses.\\n```\\n\\nThe marker propagates through dependencies: a theorem whose proof transitively\\nuses an unfaithful declaration is itself unfaithful until the dependency is\\nreplaced by a source-faithful proof. These lighter\\nmarkers are for mathematically correct local corrections; `**Unfaithful:**` is\\nreserved for load-bearing assumptions or proof steps still missing from the\\npaper hypotheses.\\n\\n## Code Conventions\\n\\n### Imports\\n\\n- Keep imports at the top of the file\\n- One import per line\\n- Follow existing local import style\\n- Prefer the smallest correct import set, but do not churn imports unnecessarily\\n- Preserve re-export-file structure: `MIPStarRE.lean`, `MIPStarRE/LDT.lean`\\n- Before adding a new import, check whether the needed declaration already\\n  comes from an existing local re-export import\\n\\n### File structure\\n\\nEvery `.lean` file must have:\\n\\n1. imports\\n2. a module docstring starting with `/-!` (title, main definitions, references)\\n3. namespace / opens / variables\\n4. declarations\\n\\n### Formatting\\n\\n- **Line length**: max 100 characters\\n- **Spacing**: spaces around `:` and `:=`\\n- **`by` placement**: at end of the preceding line (`... := by`), never on its\\n  own line\\n- **Indentation**: 2 spaces for proof body; 4 spaces for continuation of\\n  theorem statement\\n- **Top-level commands**: flush-left\\n- Avoid orphaned parentheses. Prefer readable multiline formatting over dense\\n  tactic blocks.\\n\\n### Naming conventions\\n\\nFollow Mathlib naming plus project-local conventions:\\n\\n- Theorems / proofs / proposition-valued terms: `snake_case`\\n- Structures / inductives / classes / Prop names / Type names: `UpperCamelCase`\\n- Functions / non-Prop terms: `lowerCamelCase`\\n- Use American English spelling in declaration names\\n\\nProject-preferred variable names:\\n\\n- `q` — alphabet size / finite field order\\n- `n`, `m` — dimensions\\n- `σ` — strategies\\n- `P` — projective measurements\\n- `G` — graphs (hypercube expansion)\\n\\nFor full details, see the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_style` references.\\n\\n### Types and signatures\\n\\n- Give explicit types for declaration arguments\\n- Give explicit return types for definitions\\n- Do not rely on auto-implicit variables (forbidden by `relaxedAutoImplicit`)\\n- Prefer existing project structures and Mathlib-compatible types over ad hoc\\n  wrappers\\n- Be skeptical of scaffolding that compiles but cannot support real proofs later\\n\\n### Documentation\\n\\nRequired:\\n\\n- **Module docstrings** for every file — `/-! # Title ... ## References ... -/`\\n- **Docstrings** on every `def`, `structure`, `class`, and significant `theorem`\\n- Mathematical prose in Lean docstrings and comments should follow\\n  `docs/mathematical_language.md`\\n- Cite blueprint nodes by their stable LaTeX label, for example blueprint\\n  `lem:cl-concat`. Do not store blueprint line numbers in Lean docstrings. When\\n  reviewing, derive the current span with\\n  `python3 scripts/blueprint_citations.py resolve lem:cl-concat`.\\n- Cite paper mirrors by a paper label when one exists, or by a repository path\\n  plus a narrow anchored passage when the source has no suitable label. Paper\\n  mirror line ranges are acceptable because those mirrors are immutable.\\n\\nWhen formalizing a statement from the blueprint, add corresponding `\\\\lean{...}`\\nand `\\\\leanok` tags in the relevant `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file.\\n\\n## Proof Engineering\\n\\n### Search before proving\\n\\n- Prefer existing Mathlib lemmas\\n- Reuse local API from `Quantum/` and `LDT/Basic/`\\n- Use file-local helper lemmas only when they genuinely reduce duplication\\n- Scout Mathlib first: `exact?`, `apply?`, `#find?`, grep Mathlib source\\n- See `audits/` for chapter-by-chapter Mathlib dependency analysis\\n\\n### Mathlib integration\\n\\nThe project depends heavily on Mathlib for finite-dimensional complex matrices,\\nHermitian/PSD operators, and spectral theory. When proving lemmas:\\n\\n- Reuse existing Mathlib lemmas rather than reproving\\n- Prefer Mathlib types over custom definitions\\n- Do not re-declare standard Mathlib lemmas (e.g., custom matrix transpose\\n  lemmas when `Matrix.transpose_*` exists)\\n\\nFor a pedagogical register of external lemmas not explained in the paper,\\nsee `docs/external-lemmas-pedagogy.md`. This includes Schwartz–Zippel,\\nFourier orthogonality, Cauchy–Schwarz for approximate measurements, CFC,\\nand external result statements (Polishchuk–Spielman, Raz–Safra).\\n\\nFor the policy on temporary conditional scaffolding and blueprint\\nsynchronization, see `docs/formalization-patterns.md`.\\n\\n### Validation ladder\\n\\n1. `lake env lean path/to/File.lean`\\n2. `lake build`\\n\\nDo not jump straight to full builds for every small edit.\\n\\n### Lean-specific advice\\n\\n- Prefer small, composable lemmas over giant fragile proofs\\n- Reuse `SubMeas`, `Measurement`, tensor-placement, PSD, and trace lemmas\\n  already in the repo\\n- Check `docs/api_surface.md` for useful obligation-closing lemmas\\n- If changing statements, confirm against paper and blueprint first\\n- Never add axioms or weaken statements without explicit justification\\n\\n## Mathematical Documentation Style\\n\\nWrite repository prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists.  "body": "### Motivation\n\nThe owner's capacity is not a fact of the run; it changes during it. One to three endpoints,\neach with one or two API keys, each key's concurrency limit somewhere between 5 and 40 and\nmoving while work is going on: the endpoint's admin reassigns slots, the owner wins them\nback, a key becomes invalid, a key runs out of quota. On 2026-09-12 every one of those\nevents reached the pipeline as a message to a session that had to be idle to receive it, and\nthe caps were then edited by hand ten times.\n\nW1 (#550, this PR's base) fixed the *start* of a run: one brief, one mode file, one accessor.\nIt did not fix the *middle*. The brief is one-shot by design, so changing a ceiling meant\nre-applying it and re-seeding every derived value, and nothing at all let the owner add or\nretire a key. Worse, two key names were hard-coded through the layer \u2014\n`account_router.ACCOUNTS = (\"primary\", \"second\")`, `run_mode.ACCOUNT_NAMES`, `dispatch.sh`'s\n`for account in primary second`, the `--account` choices, the second key's `CODEX_HOME` as an\n`if` rather than a field \u2014 so a third key could not be expressed at all.\n\nThis PR makes the set of usable keys and their ceilings a **live, owner-owned file** that the\nrunning pipeline re-reads, editable from a shell or from GitHub, with no prompt to any\nsession and no re-brief.\n\n### Description\n\n**1. One live file.** `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/watchdog/accounts.json` is the source of truth\nfor admission: one entry per key, `{name, label, endpoint, codex_home, ceiling,\nexternal_reserved, enabled, note}`, any number of endpoints and keys. **No key value is ever\nstored in it** \u2014 an entry names the codex home the key lives in, which only the owner\ntouches. `local/bin/accounts_file.py` owns the schema, the validation, the atomic write\n(temp file + `os.replace`, validation strictly before it, so a reader a millisecond later\nnever sees a half-file), the `watchdog/capacity/accounts.log` audit line and the `ACCOUNTS:`\ndirective grammar \u2014 so the CLI and the GitHub channel cannot disagree about what a valid\nentry is. `run_mode.py apply` **seeds** the file from the brief when it is absent and never\noverwrites an existing one; where it exists, it is what `apply` reads, so re-applying a brief\nto change the speed tier cannot undo an hour of ceiling edits.\n\n**2. Re-read every tick, with ceiling semantics.** The capacity controller loads it on every\ntick and `account_router.py` on every reservation (at most 60 s stale). `ceiling` is a\nceiling and never a target: the AIMD discovery is unchanged below it and may never exceed\n`ceiling - external_reserved`. Lowering it takes effect at the next tick; raising it lets the\nadditive creep continue rather than jumping the cap. `enabled: false` and a removed entry are\ncap 0 with no probe \u2014 and the router reads the flag directly, which closes the up-to-60-second\nwindow between the owner's edit and the controller's tick. An **invalid** file is a hard,\nnamed failure with the cap files untouched; falling back to the brief would restore the\nceiling the owner has just lowered.\n\n**3. Measured health, with a reason.** `auth` (401/403, invalid key) and\n`insufficient_balance` (`INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`, quota) are marked `\"disables\": true` in\n`local/capacity-policy.json` and take the key to cap 0 at the **first** occurrence \u2014 a `401`\nis not a statistic, and no amount of AIMD makes an invalid key valid. `endpoint_5xx` keeps\nits 3-in-120 s threshold. Both record `reason` and `disabled_by`, in the per-account health\nfiles and in the new `watchdog/capacity/health.json` (one document for every key). The way\nback is the same half-open, single-flight, read-only probe restoring cap **1**, with the\nkey-invalid backoff starting at five minutes rather than thirty seconds.\n`capacity_controller.py probe [ACCOUNT]` runs it on demand.\n\n**4. Two owner touchpoints, neither of them a prompt.**\n`results/telemetry/owner-tools/accounts.sh list|get|set|enable|disable|add|remove|probe|log`\nis the shell one, installed by the versioned installer. For when there is no shell, a comment\non the owner inbox issue in the form `ACCOUNTS: <name> ceiling=<n> [reserved=<n>]\n[enabled=true|false]` is applied by a sixth janitor pass (`local/bin/accounts_inbox.py`) and\nanswered with one reply per comment saying exactly what took effect. Only the repository\nowner login recorded in `local/README.md` is applied; anyone else's comment is answered with\na `rejected:` line naming them, so an attempt is visible rather than silent. A comment is\napplied **exactly once** (the reply carries its comment id), so a sweep every minute cannot\nre-apply a ceiling the owner has since changed at the shell. The channel carries `ceiling`,\n`reserved`, `enabled` and `note` only: an endpoint or a codex home is a path on the host and\nis set at the shell, where a typo cannot travel through a public comment. replacement for the parent project's GitHub Actions layer. Architecture and

```
issue  →  branch + worktree  →  agent session(s)  →  local CI  →  review
  →  (auto-fix loop)  →  merge gate  →  main  →  cache warmer refresh
```

   a GitHub issue and prints its number; `--parent N` attaches it as a native
   sub-issue. Record each prerequisite, including one already closed, with

   safe to repeat. The brief for the issue goes in `local/briefs/`.

   `.worktrees/`, run `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh` there, then
   `local/bin/pr_open.py --branch issue-<number>-slug --title "..." --body-file pr.md --issue N` (the body follows the PR template in `local/protocols/issues-prs.md`),

   lands in `results/telemetry/`. Lease-backed native descendants are retired;
   `protocols/sessions.md` retains their history separately.
4. **CI**: `local/bin/ci.sh PPPP` (build via hot cache + audits + blueprint
   checks) → per-step `local-ci/*` statuses and the manifest PR comment.
5. **Review**: `local/bin/review.sh PPPP` — runs only after green CI; publishes
   one exact-head COMMENT review plus the `local-review/summary` status.
6. **Auto-fix** (optional, the repository's auto-fix label on the PR):
   `local/bin/autofix.sh PPPP --mode auto`, capped, serialized.
7. **Merge**: `local/bin/pr_merge.py PPPP` — the gate; refuses on red CI,
   missing review, or unresolved findings, and merges via GitHub with the
   exact-SHA guard. Then pokes the cache warmer.
8. **Housekeeping / site**: `local/bin/housekeeping.sh all`,
   `local/bin/site.sh all`.

**Choosing the next packet.** `local/bin/ready_packets.py` walks the packet tree
under the Stage 4.3 tracker #47 — chapter trackers, their packets, and nested
chains such as Magic Square rigidity — and prints the open leaf packets whose
GitHub issue dependencies (`blocked_by`) are all closed. `--all` adds the
blocked packets with their open blockers, `--json` feeds the lane launcher, and

## The owner's live files

Two runtime files are the **owner's**, not the pipeline's. Nothing in `local/bin`
overwrites either of them, and every tool reads them rather than carrying a copy.

| File (under `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/watchdog/`) | Written by | Read by |
|---|---|---|
| `run-brief.json` | the owner, once per run | `local/bin/run_mode.py apply` |

use them — one entry per key, any number of endpoints and keys, and no key value ever

Retired useful-work queue: [historical protocol](protocols/useful-queue.md).

 "body": "### Motivation\n\nThe owner's capacity is not a fact of the run; it changes during it. One to three endpoints,\neach with one or two API keys, each key's concurrency limit somewhere between 5 and 40 and\nmoving while work is going on: the endpoint's admin reassigns slots, the owner wins them\nback, a key becomes invalid, a key runs out of quota. On 2026-09-12 every one of those\nevents reached the pipeline as a message to a session that had to be idle to receive it, and\nthe caps were then edited by hand ten times.\n\nW1 (#550, this PR's base) fixed the *start* of a run: one brief, one mode file, one accessor.\nIt did not fix the *middle*. The brief is one-shot by design, so changing a ceiling meant\nre-applying it and re-seeding every derived value, and nothing at all let the owner add or\nretire a key. Worse, two key names were hard-coded through the layer \u2014\n`account_router.ACCOUNTS = (\"primary\", \"second\")`, `run_mode.ACCOUNT_NAMES`, `dispatch.sh`'s\n`for account in primary second`, the `--account` choices, the second key's `CODEX_HOME` as an\n`if` rather than a field \u2014 so a third key could not be expressed at all.\n\nThis PR makes the set of usable keys and their ceilings a **live, owner-owned file** that the\nrunning pipeline re-reads, editable from a shell or from GitHub, with no prompt to any\nsession and no re-brief.\n\n### Description\n\n**1. One live file.** `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/watchdog/accounts.json` is the source of truth\nfor admission: one entry per key, `{name, label, endpoint, codex_home, ceiling,\nexternal_reserved, enabled, note}`, any number of endpoints and keys. **No key value is ever\nstored in it** \u2014 an entry names the codex home the key lives in, which only the owner\ntouches. `local/bin/accounts_file.py` owns the schema, the validation, the atomic write\n(temp file + `os.replace`, validation strictly before it, so a reader a millisecond later\nnever sees a half-file), the `watchdog/capacity/accounts.log` audit line and the `ACCOUNTS:`\ndirective grammar \u2014 so the CLI and the GitHub channel cannot disagree about what a valid\nentry is. `run_mode.py apply` **seeds** the file from the brief when it is absent and never\noverwrites an existing one; where it exists, it is what `apply` reads, so re-applying a brief\nto change the speed tier cannot undo an hour of ceiling edits.\n\n**2. Re-read every tick, with ceiling semantics.** The capacity controller loads it on every\ntick and `account_router.py` on every reservation (at most 60 s stale). `ceiling` is a\nceiling and never a target: the AIMD discovery is unchanged below it and may never exceed\n`ceiling - external_reserved`. Lowering it takes effect at the next tick; raising it lets the\nadditive creep continue rather than jumping the cap. `enabled: false` and a removed entry are\ncap 0 with no probe \u2014 and the router reads the flag directly, which closes the up-to-60-second\nwindow between the owner's edit and the controller's tick. An **invalid** file is a hard,\nnamed failure with the cap files untouched; falling back to the brief would restore the\nceiling the owner has just lowered.\n\n**3. Measured health, with a reason.** `auth` (401/403, invalid key) and\n`insufficient_balance` (`INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE`, quota) are marked `\"disables\": true` in\n`local/capacity-policy.json` and take the key to cap 0 at the **first** occurrence \u2014 a `401`\nis not a statistic, and no amount of AIMD makes an invalid key valid. `endpoint_5xx` keeps\nits 3-in-120 s threshold. Both record `reason` and `disabled_by`, in the per-account health\nfiles and in the new `watchdog/capacity/health.json` (one document for every key). The way\nback is the same half-open, single-flight, read-only probe restoring cap **1**, with the\nkey-invalid backoff starting at five minutes rather than thirty seconds.\n`capacity_controller.py probe [ACCOUNT]` runs it on demand.\n\n**4. Two owner touchpoints, neither of them a prompt.**\n`results/telemetry/owner-tools/accounts.sh list|get|set|enable|disable|add|remove|probe|log`\nis the shell one, installed by the versioned installer. For when there is no shell, a comment\non the owner inbox issue in the form `ACCOUNTS: <name> ceiling=<n> [reserved=<n>]\n[enabled=true|false]` is applied by a sixth janitor pass (`local/bin/accounts_inbox.py`) and\nanswered with one reply per comment saying exactly what took effect. Only the repository\nowner login recorded in `local/README.md` is applied; anyone else's comment is answered with\na `rejected:` line naming them, so an attempt is visible rather than silent. A comment is\napplied **exactly once** (the reply carries its comment id), so a sweep every minute cannot\nre-apply a ceiling the owner has since changed at the shell. The channel carries `ceiling`,\n`reserved`, `enabled` and `note` only: an endpoint or a codex home is a path on the host and\nis set at the shell, where a typo cannot travel through a public comment. Comment bodies stay\nuntrusted text \u2014 only `ACCOUNTS:` lines are read, every value is validated before anything is\nwritten, and nothi\n\n---\nCloses #555\n",

```
issue  →  branch + worktree  →  agent session(s)  →  local CI  →  review
  →  (auto-fix loop)  →  merge gate  →  main  →  cache warmer refresh

   sub-issue. Record each prerequisite, including one already closed, with

   `protocols/sessions.md` retains their history separately.
4. **CI**: `local/bin/ci.sh PPPP` (build via hot cache + audits + blueprint
   checks) → per-step `local-ci/*` statuses and the manifest PR comment.
5. **Review**: `local/bin/review.sh PPPP` — runs only after green CI; publishes
   one exact-head COMMENT review plus the `local-review/summary` status.
6. **Auto-fix** (optional, the repository's auto-fix label on the PR):
   `local/bin/autofix.sh PPPP --mode auto`, capped, serialized.
7. **Merge**: `local/bin/pr_merge.py PPPP` — the gate; refuses on red CI,
   missing review, or unresolved findings, and merges via GitHub with the
   exact-SHA guard. Then pokes the cache warmer.
8. **Housekeeping / site**: `local/bin/housekeeping.sh all`,
   `local/bin/site.sh all`.

**Choosing the next packet.** `local/bin/ready_packets.py` walks the packet tree
under the Stage 4.3 tracker #47 — chapter trackers, their packets, and nested
chains such as Magic Square rigidity — and prints the open leaf packets whose
GitHub issue dependencies (`blocked_by`) are all closed. `--all` adds the

## The owner's live files

Two runtime files are the **owner's**, not the pipeline's. Nothing in `local/bin`
overwrites either of them, and every tool reads them rather than carrying a copy.

| File (under `~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/watchdog/`) | Written by | Read by |
|---|---|---|
| `run-brief.json` | the owner, once per run | `local/bin/run_mode.py apply` |
| `accounts.json` | the owner, at any moment | the capacity controller and `account_router.py`, every tick and every reservation |

use them — one entry per key, any number of endpoints and keys, and no key value ever

Retired useful-work queue: [historical protocol](protocols/useful-queue.md).

These should still be reviewed and\\ndocumented if they are mathematically load-bearing.  The forbidden pattern is\\ndifferent: moving an unproved step of the proof into the theorem statement, such\\nas a `BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`,\\n`Producer`, generic `Hypotheses`, or generic `Assumptions` assumption that the\\npaper theorem does not assume.  These assumptions\\nshould not be introduced merely to keep a file compiling or to avoid a `sorry`;\\nthey require explicit mathematical justification and a planned discharge.\\n\\nFor the current LDT final theorem, `mainFormal` is reserved for the statement of\\n`\\\\Cref{thm:main-formal}`: from a projective strategy passing the low individual\\ndegree test, it produces the three final consistency conclusions. The corresponding paper-aligned version should remain\\nvisible, even if its proof is temporarily unfinished during repair.\\n\\nEvery agent changing a paper-labelled theorem must finish with a statement\\nintegrity audit:\\n\\n- paper assumptions;\\n- Lean assumptions;\\n- paper conclusion;\\n- Lean conclusion;\\n- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened\\n  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.\\n\\n### Paper-realignment mode\\n\\nWhen a theorem, definition, or hypothesis field has already drifted away from\\n`references/ldt-paper/`, a repair PR may temporarily reintroduce `sorry` in\\norder to restore the source-faithful statement.  In this mode, statement\\nfaithfulness is the first invariant: keeping a divergent proof intact merely to\\navoid `sorry` preserves a theorem that the paper does not state.\\n\\nPaper-realignment mode is narrow.  It applies only to edits whose purpose is to\\nremove wrong hypotheses, delete divergent fields, restore a paper theorem\\nstatement, or replace a conditional theorem by a paper-facing statement plus a\\nnamed proof obligation.  Such a PR must:\\n\\n1. cite the paper passage by label or line range in the relevant docstring;\\n2. cite the paper-gap note or tracking issue that records the divergence;\\n3. identify every introduced or retained `sorry` and the construction theorem,\\n   proof-obligation theorem, or source-faithful lemma expected to discharge it;\\n4. avoid unrelated refactors, notation changes, or proof-engineering churn.\\n\\nDuring paper realignment, every restated definition, hypothesis field, or\\npaper-facing theorem must have a docstring that lets a reviewer tell whether\\nthe statement is present in the paper or is a Lean-only proof obligation.  A\\nname such as `Bridge`, `Residual`, `Repair`, `Package`, `Input`, or `Producer`\\nis not by itself a mathematical source citation.\\n\\n### Unfaithful dependency markers\\n\\nA theorem or lemma is **unfaithful** when its proof relies on a hypothesis,\\nhelper, bridge, residual, repair input, or conditional theorem that is known not\\nto follow from the cited paper statement.  This includes the case where the\\npublic theorem statement is source-shaped but the proof calls a conditional\\nhelper whose load-bearing hypothesis is not yet derived from the paper\\nhypotheses.\\n\\nSuch a declaration must carry a docstring section beginning with\\n`**Unfaithful:**`.  The marker must name the load-bearing deviation, cite the\\npaper-gap note or issue that documents it, and state the planned discharge.  A\\nminimal form is:\\n\\n```text\\n**Unfaithful:** This proof currently relies on `<hypothesis or helper>`,\\nwhich is not derived from `<paper label or line range>`.  Documented in\\n`docs/paper-gaps/<note>.tex` or issue `#N`.  Elimination: prove\\n`<construction theorem>` from the paper hypotheses.\\n```\\n\\nThe marker propagates through dependencies: a theorem whose proof transitively\\nuses an unfaithful declaration is itself unfaithful until the dependency is\\nreplaced by a source-faithful proof.  Remove the marker only when the cited\\ndeviation has been discharged.\\n\\nNot every discrepancy requires the full `**Unfaithful:**` marker. These lighter\\nmarkers are for mathematically correct local corrections; `**Unfaithful:**` is\\nreserved for load-bearing assumptions or proof steps still missing from the\\npaper hypotheses.\\n\\n## Code Conventions\\n\\n### Imports\\n\\n- Keep imports at the top of the file\\n- One import per line\\n- Follow existing local import style\\n- Prefer the smallest correct import set, but do not churn imports unnecessarily\\n- Preserve re-export-file structure: `MIPStarRE.lean`, `MIPStarRE/LDT.lean`\\n- Before adding a new import, check whether the needed declaration already\\n  comes from an existing local re-export import\\n\\n### File structure\\n\\nEvery `.lean` file must have:\\n\\n1. imports\\n2. a module docstring starting with `/-!` (title, main definitions, references)\\n3. namespace / opens / variables\\n4. declarations\\n\\n### Formatting\\n\\n- **Line length**: max 100 characters\\n- **Spacing**: spaces around `:` and `:=`\\n- **`by` placement**: at end of the preceding line (`... := by`), never on its\\n  own line\\n- **Indentation**: 2 spaces for proof body; 4 spaces for continuation of\\n  theorem statement\\n- **Top-level commands**: flush-left\\n- Avoid orphaned parentheses. Prefer readable multiline formatting over dense\\n  tactic blocks.\\n\\n### Naming conventions\\n\\nFollow Mathlib naming plus project-local conventions:\\n\\n- Theorems / proofs / proposition-valued terms: `snake_case`\\n- Structures / inductives / classes / Prop names / Type names: `UpperCamelCase`\\n- Functions / non-Prop terms: `lowerCamelCase`\\n- Use American English spelling in declaration names\\n\\nProject-preferred variable names:\\n\\n- `q` — alphabet size / finite field order\\n- `n`, `m` — dimensions\\n- `σ` — strategies\\n- `P` — projective measurements\\n- `G` — graphs (hypercube expansion)\\n\\nFor full details, see the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_style` references.\\n\\n### Types and signatures\\n\\n- Give explicit types for declaration arguments\\n- Give explicit return types for definitions\\n- Do not rely on auto-implicit variables (forbidden by `relaxedAutoImplicit`)\\n- Prefer existing project structures and Mathlib-compatible types over ad hoc\\n  wrappers\\n- Be skeptical of scaffolding that compiles but cannot support real proofs later\\n\\n### Documentation\\n\\nRequired:\\n\\n- **Module docstrings** for every file — `/-! # Title ... ## References ... -/`\\n- **Docstrings** on every `def`, `structure`, `class`, and significant `theorem`\\n- Mathematical prose in Lean docstrings and comments should follow\\n  `docs/mathematical_language.md`\\n- Cite blueprint nodes by their stable LaTeX label, for example blueprint\\n  `lem:cl-concat`. Do not store blueprint line numbers in Lean docstrings. Paper\\n  mirror line ranges are acceptable because those mirrors are immutable.\\n\\nWhen formalizing a statement from the blueprint, add corresponding `\\\\lean{...}`\\nand `\\\\leanok` tags in the relevant `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` file.\\n\\n## Proof Engineering\\n\\n### Search before proving\\n\\n- Prefer existing Mathlib lemmas\\n- Reuse local API from `Quantum/` and `LDT/Basic/`\\n- Use file-local helper lemmas only when they genuinely reduce duplication\\n- Scout Mathlib first: `exact?`, `apply?`, `#find?`, grep Mathlib source\\n- See `audits/` for chapter-by-chapter Mathlib dependency analysis\\n\\n### Mathlib integration\\n\\nThe project depends heavily on Mathlib for finite-dimensional complex matrices,\\nHermitian/PSD operators, and spectral theory. When proving lemmas:\\n\\n- Reuse existing Mathlib lemmas rather than reproving\\n- Prefer Mathlib types over custom definitions\\n- Do not re-declare standard Mathlib lemmas (e.g., custom matrix transpose\\n  lemmas when `Matrix.transpose_*` exists)\\n\\nFor a pedagogical register of external lemmas not explained in the paper,\\nsee `docs/external-lemmas-pedagogy.md`. This includes Schwartz–Zippel,\\nFourier orthogonality, Cauchy–Schwarz for approximate measurements, CFC,\\nand external result statements (Polishchuk–Spielman, Raz–Safra).\\n\\nFor the policy on temporary conditional scaffolding and blueprint\\nsynchronization, see `docs/formalization-patterns.md`.\\n\\n### Validation ladder\\n\\n1. `lake env lean path/to/File.lean`\\n2. `lake build`\\n\\nDo not jump straight to full builds for every small edit.\\n\\n### Lean-specific advice\\n\\n- Prefer small, composable lemmas over giant fragile proofs\\n- Reuse `SubMeas`, `Measurement`, tensor-placement, PSD, and trace lemmas\\n  already in the repo\\n- Check `docs/api_surface.md` for useful obligation-closing lemmas\\n- If changing statements, confirm against paper and blueprint first\\n- Never add axioms or weaken statements without explicit justification\\n\\n## Mathematical Documentation Style\\n\\nWrite repository prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists. Prefer a\\nclear, precise, and unhurried expository style: introduce the object under\\ndiscussion, state the mathematical relation being used, distinguish hypotheses\\nfrom conclusions, and avoid informal process language when a standard\\nmathematical phrase is available.\\n\\nWhen writing docstrings, audit notes, PR descriptions, or blueprint-adjacent\\ncomments, use terminology from the standard mathematical literature, the LDT\\npaper, and the local formalization. For documentation of discrepancies\\nbetween the cited paper, the blueprint, and Lean, follow\\n`docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex`. In particular, such notes should be\\nmathematical prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists who have not\\nread the issue discussion: introduce notation, state the cited assertion,\\nisolate the calculation or logical obstruction, compare with the blueprint and\\nLean statement, and give a clear verdict. If the cited assertion is\\nfalse and a counterexample is available, explain the counterexample in prose and\\nuse any Lean declaration only as verification.\\n\\n## Proof Integrity\\n\\n### Blockers (must be resolved before merge)\\n\\nSee the lean-conventions `PROOF_INTEGRITY` reference and `docs/project_conventions.md` for the full catalog.\\n\\n**Direct proof holes**: `sorry`, `admit`\\n\\n**Kernel / type system bypasses**: `native_decide`, `unsafeCast`, `unsafeCoerce`,\\n`lcProof`, `ofReduceBool`, `ofReduceNat`\\n\\n**Axiom smuggling**: unjustified `axiom` declarations\\n\\n**Circular reasoning**: proofs that assume the statement being proved as a local\\nhypothesis, or helper lemmas that essentially restate the main goal.\\n\\n**Castle-in-the-air (ungrounded proofs)**: custom re-declarations of standard\\nMathlib lemmas; `axiom` or `sorry`-based helpers for facts already in Mathlib;\\nchains of custom lemmas that never bottom out in Mathlib or Lean core.\\n\\n**Scaffolding that blocks real formalization**: definitions or theorem statements\\nthat do not faithfully represent the actual mathematics, making them impossible\\nto connect to real Mathlib-based proofs. These should still be reviewed and\\\\ndocumented if they are mathematically load-bearing.  The forbidden pattern is\\\\ndifferent: moving an unproved step of the proof into the theorem statement, such\\\\nas a `BridgeHypotheses`, `Input`, `Residual`, `Package`, `RepairInput`,\\\\n`Producer`, generic `Hypotheses`, or generic `Assumptions` assumption that the\\\\npaper theorem does not assume.  These assumptions\\\\nshould not be introduced merely to keep a file compiling or to avoid a `sorry`;\\\\nthey require explicit mathematical justification and a planned discharge.\\\\n\\\\nFor the current LDT final theorem, `mainFormal` is reserved for the statement of\\\\n`\\\\\\\\Cref{thm:main-formal}`: from a projective strategy passing the low individual\\\\ndegree test, it produces the three final consistency conclusions.  A theorem\\\\nwith an extra hypothesis such as\\\\n`hbaseBridge : ... → MainFormalRepairedBridgeHypotheses ...` is temporary\\\\nscaffolding at best; it must not be the declaration advertised as\\\\n`thm:main-formal`.  The corresponding paper-aligned version should remain\\\\nvisible, even if its proof is temporarily unfinished during repair.\\\\n\\\\nEvery agent changing a paper-labelled theorem must finish with a statement\\\\nintegrity audit:\\\\n\\\\n- paper assumptions;\\\\n- Lean assumptions;\\\\n- paper conclusion;\\\\n- Lean conclusion;\\\\n- verdict: exact, faithful boundary hypotheses, extra assumptions, weakened\\\\n  conclusion, or strengthened conclusion.\\\\n\\\\n### Paper-realignment mode\\\\n\\\\nWhen a theorem, definition, or hypothesis field has already drifted away from\\\\n`references/ldt-paper/`, a repair PR may temporarily reintroduce `sorry` in\\\\norder to restore the source-faithful statement.  In this mode, statement\\\\nfaithfulness is the first invariant: keeping a divergent proof intact merely to\\\\navoid `sorry` preserves a theorem that the paper does not state.\\\\n\\\\nPaper-realignment mode is narrow. Such a PR must:\\\\n\\\\n1. cite the paper passage by label or line range in the relevant docstring;\\\\n2. cite the paper-gap note or tracking issue that records the divergence;\\\\n3. identify every introduced or retained `sorry` and the construction theorem,\\\\n   proof-obligation theorem, or source-faithful lemma expected to discharge it;\\\\n4. avoid unrelated refactors, notation changes, or proof-engineering churn.\\\\n\\\\nDuring paper realignment, every restated definition, hypothesis field, or\\\\npaper-facing theorem must have a docstring that lets a reviewer tell whether\\\\nthe statement is present in the paper or is a Lean-only proof obligation.  A\\\\nname such as `Bridge`, `Residual`, `Repair`, `Package`, `Input`, or `Producer`\\\\nis not by itself a mathematical source citation.\\\\n\\\\n### Unfaithful dependency markers\\\\n\\\\nA theorem or lemma is **unfaithful** when its proof relies on a hypothesis,\\\\nhelper, bridge, residual, repair input, or conditional theorem that is known not\\\\nto follow from the cited paper statement.  This includes the case where the\\\\npublic theorem statement is source-shaped but the proof calls a conditional\\\\nhelper whose load-bearing hypothesis is not yet derived from the paper\\\\nhypotheses.\\\\n\\\\nSuch a declaration must carry a docstring section beginning with\\\\n`**Unfaithful:**`. These lighter\\\\nmarkers are for mathematically correct local corrections; `**Unfaithful:**` is\\\\nreserved for load-bearing assumptions or proof steps still missing from the\\\\npaper hypotheses.\\\\n\\\\n## Code Conventions\\\\n\\\\n### Imports\\\\n\\\\n- Keep imports at the top of the file\\\\n- One import per line\\\\n- Follow existing local import style\\\\n- Prefer the smallest correct import set, but do not churn imports unnecessarily\\\\n- Preserve re-export-file structure: `MIPStarRE.lean`, `MIPStarRE/LDT.lean`\\\\n- Before adding a new import, check whether the needed declaration already\\\\n  comes from an existing local re-export import\\\\n\\\\n### File structure\\\\n\\\\nEvery `.lean` file must have:\\\\n\\\\n1. imports\\\\n2. a module docstring starting with `/-!` (title, main definitions, references)\\\\n3. namespace / opens / variables\\\\n4. declarations\\\\n\\\\n### Formatting\\\\n\\\\n- **Line length**: max 100 characters\\\\n- **Spacing**: spaces around `:` and `:=`\\\\n- **`by` placement**: at end of the preceding line (`... := by`), never on its\\\\n  own line\\\\n- **Indentation**: 2 spaces for proof body; 4 spaces for continuation of\\\\n  theorem statement\\\\n- **Top-level commands**: flush-left\\\\n- Avoid orphaned parentheses. Prefer readable multiline formatting over dense\\\\n  tactic blocks.\\\\n\\\\n### Naming conventions\\\\n\\\\nFollow Mathlib naming plus project-local conventions:\\\\n\\\\n- Theorems / proofs / proposition-valued terms: `snake_case`\\\\n- Structures / inductives / classes / Prop names / Type names: `UpperCamelCase`\\\\n- Functions / non-Prop terms: `lowerCamelCase`\\\\n- Use American English spelling in declaration names\\\\n\\\\nProject-preferred variable names:\\\\n\\\\n- `q` — alphabet size / finite field order\\\\n- `n`, `m` — dimensions\\\\n- `σ` — strategies\\\\n- `P` — projective measurements\\\\n- `G` — graphs (hypercube expansion)\\\\n\\\\nFor full details, see the lean-conventions `MATHLIB_naming` and `MATHLIB_style` references.\\\\n\\\\n### Types and signatures\\\\n\\\\n- Give explicit types for declaration arguments\\\\n- Give explicit return types for definitions\\\\n- Do not rely on auto-implicit variables (forbidden by `relaxedAutoImplicit`)\\\\n- Prefer existing project structures and Mathlib-compatible types over ad hoc\\\\n  wrappers\\\\n- Be skeptical of scaffolding that compiles but cannot support real proofs later\\\\n\\\\n### Documentation\\\\n\\\\nRequired:\\\\n\\\\n- **Module docstrings** for every file — `/-! # Title ... ## References ... -/`\\\\n- **Docstrings** on every `def`, `structure`, `class`, and significant `theorem`\\\\n- Mathematical prose in Lean docstrings and comments should follow\\\\n  `docs/mathematical_language.md`\\\\n- Cite blueprint nodes by their stable LaTeX label, for example blueprint\\\\n  `lem:cl-concat`. When proving lemmas:\\\\n\\\\n- Reuse existing Mathlib lemmas rather than reproving\\\\n- Prefer Mathlib types over custom definitions\\\\n- Do not re-declare standard Mathlib lemmas (e.g., custom matrix transpose\\\\n  lemmas when `Matrix.transpose_*` exists)\\\\n\\\\nFor a pedagogical register of external lemmas not explained in the paper,\\\\nsee `docs/external-lemmas-pedagogy.md`. This includes Schwartz–Zippel,\\\\nFourier orthogonality, Cauchy–Schwarz for approximate measurements, CFC,\\\\nand external result statements (Polishchuk–Spielman, Raz–Safra).\\\\n\\\\nFor the policy on temporary conditional scaffolding and blueprint\\\\nsynchronization, see `docs/formalization-patterns.md`.\\\\n\\\\n### Validation ladder\\\\n\\\\n1. `lake env lean path/to/File.lean`\\\\n2. `lake build`\\\\n\\\\nDo not jump straight to full builds for every small edit.\\\\n\\\\n### Lean-specific advice\\\\n\\\\n- Prefer small, composable lemmas over giant fragile proofs\\\\n- Reuse `SubMeas`, `Measurement`, tensor-placement, PSD, and trace lemmas\\\\n  already in the repo\\\\n- Check `docs/api_surface.md` for useful obligation-closing lemmas\\\\n- If changing statements, confirm against paper and blueprint first\\\\n- Never add axioms or weaken statements without explicit justification\\\\n\\\\n## Mathematical Documentation Style\\\\n\\\\nWrite repository prose for mathematicians and mathematical physicists. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reject merge results that silently discard an incoming tree change.

The pending-merge mode compares the staged index with ``HEAD``, ``MERGE_HEAD``,
and all of their best merge bases.  The committed mode performs the same check for an
existing two-parent merge commit.  Outside recorded conflicts, a path may be
absent only when the branch deleted a path that existed at the merge base.

Usage:

    merge_loss_guard.py [--repo PATH]
    merge_loss_guard.py [--repo PATH] --commit REV
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from dataclasses import dataclass
import os
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
from typing import Mapping


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class TreeEntry:
    """The mode and object identity of one non-directory tree entry."""

    mode: bytes
    object_id: bytes


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class MergeTrees:
    """The tree states needed to distinguish branch work from merge loss."""

    bases: tuple[Mapping[bytes, TreeEntry], ...]
    branch: Mapping[bytes, TreeEntry]
    incoming: Mapping[bytes, TreeEntry]
    result: Mapping[bytes, TreeEntry]
    conflicts: frozenset[bytes] = frozenset()
    automatic: Mapping[bytes, TreeEntry] | None = None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Finding:
    """One path whose incoming state was discarded by the merge result."""

    kind: str
    path: bytes


class GuardError(RuntimeError):
    """A malformed or unsupported Git state that must fail closed."""


def git_environment() -> dict[str, str]:
    """Return an environment independent of the repository invoking a hook."""

    environment = os.environ.copy()
    local_variables = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "rev-parse", "--local-env-vars"],
        check=True,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    ).stdout.splitlines()
    for variable in local_variables:
        environment.pop(variable, None)
    return environment


def run_git(repo: Path, *args: str) -> bytes:
    """Run Git in ``repo`` and return stdout, or raise an operator-facing error."""

    result = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", os.fspath(repo), *args],
        check=False,
        capture_output=True,
        env=git_environment(),
    )
    if result.returncode != 0:
        detail = os.fsdecode(result.stderr.strip() or result.stdout.strip())
        raise GuardError(f"git {' '.join(args)} failed ({result.returncode}): {detail}")
    return result.stdout


def resolve(repo: Path, revision: str) -> str:
    """Resolve ``revision`` to one commit object name."""

    return os.fsdecode(run_git(repo, "rev-parse", "--verify", f"{revision}^{{commit}}").strip())


def read_tree(repo: Path, revision: str) -> dict[bytes, TreeEntry]:
    """Read every non-directory entry from ``revision`` without path decoding."""

    entries: dict[bytes, TreeEntry] = {}
    output = run_git(repo, "ls-tree", "-rz", "--full-tree", revision)
    for record in output.split(b"\0"):
        if not record:
            continue
        metadata, path = record.split(b"\t", 1)
        mode, _kind, object_id = metadata.split(b" ", 2)
        entries[path] = TreeEntry(mode, object_id)
    return entries


def read_index(repo: Path) -> dict[bytes, TreeEntry]:
    """Read the stage-zero index used to create a pending merge commit."""

    entries: dict[bytes, TreeEntry] = {}
    output = run_git(repo, "ls-files", "--stage", "-z")
    for record in output.split(b"\0"):
        if not record:
            continue
        metadata, path = record.split(b"\t", 1)
        mode, object_id, stage = metadata.split(b" ", 2)
        if stage != b"0":
            raise GuardError(
                f"unresolved index entry at {os.fsdecode(path)!r} (stage {os.fsdecode(stage)})"
            )
        entries[path] = TreeEntry(mode, object_id)
    return entries


def read_index_state(repo: Path) -> tuple[dict[bytes, TreeEntry], frozenset[bytes]]:
    """Read clean index entries and the paths retaining conflict stages."""

    entries: dict[bytes, TreeEntry] = {}
    conflicts: set[bytes] = set()
    output = run_git(repo, "ls-files", "--stage", "-z")
    for record in output.split(b"\0"):
        if not record:
            continue
        metadata, path = record.split(b"\t", 1)
        mode, object_id, stage = metadata.split(b" ", 2)
        if stage == b"0":
            entries[path] = TreeEntry(mode, object_id)
        else:
            conflicts.add(path)
    return entries, frozenset(conflicts)


def merge_bases(repo: Path, branch: str, incoming: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Return every best merge base used to classify branch-owned changes."""

    bases = run_git(repo, "merge-base", "--all", branch, incoming).splitlines()
    if not bases:
        raise GuardError(f"no merge base for {branch} and {incoming}")
    return tuple(os.fsdecode(base) for base in bases)


def pending_merge_head(repo: Path) -> str | None:
    """Return the sole pending ``MERGE_HEAD``, or ``None`` outside a merge."""

    git_path = os.fsdecode(run_git(repo, "rev-parse", "--git-path", "MERGE_HEAD").strip())
    path = Path(git_path)
    if not path.is_absolute():
        path = repo / path
    if not path.is_file():
        return None
    heads = [line.strip() for line in path.read_text(encoding="ascii").splitlines() if line.strip()]
    if len(heads) != 1:
        raise GuardError(f"expected one MERGE_HEAD, found {len(heads)}")
    return resolve(repo, heads[0])


def pending_conflicts(repo: Path) -> frozenset[bytes]:
    """Read Git's retained conflict-path section for a resolved pending merge."""

    git_path = os.fsdecode(run_git(repo, "rev-parse", "--git-path", "MERGE_MSG").strip())
    path = Path(git_path)
    if not path.is_absolute():
        path = repo / path
    if not path.is_file():
        return frozenset()
    conflicts: set[bytes] = set()
    in_conflicts = False
    for line in path.read_bytes().splitlines():
        stripped = line.lstrip(b"#").strip()
        if stripped == b"Conflicts:":
            in_conflicts = True
            continue
        if in_conflicts:
            if not line.startswith(b"#") or not stripped:
                break
            conflicts.add(stripped)
    return frozenset(conflicts)


def reconstructed_merge(
    repo: Path, branch: str, incoming: str
) -> tuple[dict[bytes, TreeEntry], frozenset[bytes]]:
    """Recover Git's clean merge entries and conflicts in a disposable local clone."""

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="mipstarre-merge-audit-") as directory:
        clone = Path(directory) / "repo"
        clone_result = subprocess.run(
            [
                "git",
                "clone",
                "--quiet",
                "--shared",
                "--no-checkout",
                os.fspath(repo),
                os.fspath(clone),
            ],
            check=False,
            capture_output=True,
            env=git_environment(),
        )
        if clone_result.returncode != 0:
            detail = os.fsdecode(clone_result.stderr.strip() or clone_result.stdout.strip())
            raise GuardError(f"temporary local clone failed: {detail}")
        run_git(clone, "config", "user.email", "merge-loss-guard@example.invalid")
        run_git(clone, "config", "user.name", "MIPStarRE merge-loss guard")
        run_git(clone, "checkout", "--quiet", "--detach", branch)
        merge_result = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", os.fspath(clone), "merge", "--no-commit", "--no-ff", incoming],
            check=False,
            capture_output=True,
            env=git_environment(),
        )
        merge_head_output = run_git(clone, "rev-parse", "--git-path", "MERGE_HEAD").strip()
        merge_head = Path(os.fsdecode(merge_head_output))
        if not merge_head.is_absolute():
            merge_head = clone / merge_head
        if merge_result.returncode not in (0, 1) or not merge_head.is_file():
            detail = os.fsdecode(merge_result.stderr.strip() or merge_result.stdout.strip())
            raise GuardError(f"automatic merge reconstruction failed: {detail}")
        return read_index_state(clone)


def pending_trees(repo: Path) -> tuple[MergeTrees, tuple[str, ...], str, str]:
    """Load a pending merge's base, pre-merge branch, incoming, and index trees."""

    incoming = pending_merge_head(repo)
    if incoming is None:
        raise GuardError("no merge is in progress")
    branch = resolve(repo, "HEAD")
    bases = merge_bases(repo, branch, incoming)
    automatic = None
    conflicts = pending_conflicts(repo)
    if len(bases) > 1:
        automatic, reconstructed = reconstructed_merge(repo, branch, incoming)
        conflicts |= reconstructed
    trees = MergeTrees(
        bases=tuple(read_tree(repo, base) for base in bases),
        branch=read_tree(repo, branch),
        incoming=read_tree(repo, incoming),
        result=read_index(repo),
        conflicts=conflicts,
        automatic=automatic,
    )
    return trees, bases, branch, incoming


def committed_trees(
    repo: Path, revision: str
) -> tuple[MergeTrees, tuple[str, ...], str, str]:
    """Load the four trees associated with a committed two-parent merge."""

    commit = resolve(repo, revision)
    topology = os.fsdecode(run_git(repo, "rev-list", "--parents", "-n", "1", commit)).split()
    parents = topology[1:]
    if len(parents) != 2:
        raise GuardError(f"{commit} is not a two-parent merge commit")
    branch, incoming = parents
    bases = merge_bases(repo, branch, incoming)
    automatic, conflicts = (
        (None, frozenset())
        if incoming in bases
        else reconstructed_merge(repo, branch, incoming)
    )
    trees = MergeTrees(
        bases=tuple(read_tree(repo, base) for base in bases),
        branch=read_tree(repo, branch),
        incoming=read_tree(repo, incoming),

release_locks() {
  local dir
  if [ "${#LOCKS_HELD[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
    for dir in "${LOCKS_HELD[@]}"; do
      rm -f "$dir/pid" "$dir/since" 2>/dev/null || true
      rmdir "$dir" 2>/dev/null || true
    done
  fi
  LOCKS_HELD=()
}

cleanup() {
  if [ "${ACCOUNT_ROUTING:-0}" -eq 1 ]; then
    rm -f "$CACHE_ROOT/accounts/primary/$$" "$CACHE_ROOT/accounts/second/$$"
  fi
  release_locks
  # A capture file is created early to reserve the sequence number. If we die
  # before codex ever ran, release it again so the number is not burned and no
  # empty "session" is left behind for the archivist to explain.
  if [ "${CODEX_STARTED:-0}" -eq 0 ] \
    && [ -n "${CAPTURE:-}" ] && [ -f "${CAPTURE:-}" ] && [ ! -s "${CAPTURE:-}" ]; then
    rm -f "$CAPTURE"
  fi
  if [ -n "${RUN_TMPDIR:-}" ] && [ -d "${RUN_TMPDIR:-}" ]; then
    rm -rf "$RUN_TMPDIR"
  fi
}

acquire_lock() {
  # acquire_lock <name> <wait-seconds> <purpose>
  local name="$1" wait_s="$2" purpose="$3"
  local dir="$LOCK_DIR/$name.lock"
  local waited=0 owner=""
  mkdir -p "$LOCK_DIR"
  while ! mkdir "$dir" 2>/dev/null; do
    owner="$(cat "$dir/pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [ -n "$owner" ] && ! kill -0 "$owner" 2>/dev/null; then
      note "breaking stale lock $dir (pid $owner is gone)"
      rm -rf "$dir"
      continue
    fi
    if [ "$waited" -ge "$wait_s" ]; then
      die 5 "$purpose is locked by pid ${owner:-unknown} ($dir).
  Another dispatch is writing there. Wait, or pass --lock-wait SECONDS.
  Only one writing session per worktree (DESIGN.md invariant 1, single writer)."
    fi
    sleep 2
    waited=$((waited + 2))
  done
  printf '%s\n' "$$" >"$dir/pid"
  date +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z >"$dir/since"
  LOCKS_HELD[${#LOCKS_HELD[@]}]="$dir"

 "body": "### Motivation\n\nThe full speed run of 2026-09-12 (04:17Z\u201308:33Z) produced 9 merges and cost the owner\neight distinct classes of manual intervention, each of which is a defect of the workflow\nrather than of the mathematics: the concurrency limits restated five times while ~90\nworker sessions died (69 on an endpoint that had been answering 503 for an hour, the rest\nabove an unmeasured provider ceiling); repeated questions about idle slots while every\ndispatched fixer was dying at a model-policy preflight; the estimate format dictated by\nhand after multi-line prose appeared on the estimate issue; ready PRs sitting open behind\ntwo-hour timer backoffs; three lane-runner revisions hand-patched in `/tmp`; the speed\ntier switched three times by string surgery on a generated file; and a terminal stop order\nundone five minutes later by a goal keeper that had no way to know about it.\n\nThis PR is the whole of the tracker's seven work items: the owner gives **one** briefing at\nthe start of a run and afterwards receives only the half-hourly one-line estimate and prose\nprogress on the progress log. Everything else becomes an automatic mechanism, a one-file\nswitch or a self-healing loop, and every fix that lived in `/tmp` or in one host's\n`.git/config` now lives in the repository. The design document is the first comment on\n#550.\n\n### Description\n\n**1. Owner briefing, run mode and standing reports.** `local/bin/run_mode.py` validates one\n`run-brief.json` and is the single writer of `watchdog/run-mode.json` and of the derived cap\nfiles, and the single accessor for every capacity, schedule, speed and issue number, so no\nprotocol, persona or script carries a literal that can go stale. `ready_report.py` answers\n\"ready but open, and why\" hourly from daemon state, with `unexplained` as the alarm case.\n`estimate_post.py` renders the two prescribed lines and refuses any other body.\n`local/protocols/full-speed-mode.md` is the runbook and `local/personas/main.md` gains the\nStanding reports duty.\n\n**2. Dispatch and telemetry.** Provider failures are classified (`concurrency_limit`,\n`endpoint_5xx`, `retries_exhausted`, `timeout`, `task_failure`, `unknown`) and recorded with\nthe endpoint, so a capacity refusal is no longer scored like a failed proof; `dispatch.sh`\nspools its request and prompt and retries a transient class instead of dying; a branch claim\nrefuses a second writer with exit 5; the owner model override moves from a PATH-shim rewrite\n(which made the registry record a model that never ran) into the policy layer; `autofix.sh`\nstops defaulting to a model its own preflight rejects and gains the fix \u2192 CI \u2192 review loop.\n\n**3. Capacity controller.** An AIMD controller with per-endpoint health is the only writer of\nthe caps: it measures the real limit under the briefed ceiling, trips to cap 0 on a 5xx\nendpoint, recovers through one half-open read-only probe, subtracts declared external\nconsumers, and carries the measurement into the next run.\n\n**4. Operator tools.** One versioned installer with a hash manifest that refuses to overwrite\na hand patch; one `owner-pause.sh` whose every phase is clamped to the briefed deadline and\nwhich releases queued dispatches rather than killing them; one `owner-resume.sh` that\nrestores from the recorded state only; one `owner-say.sh` whose terminal mode holds the goal\nbefore it speaks.\n\n**5. Merge daemon and lane runner, promoted.** Honest names in the repository, failure markers\nthat carry a class and clear on an observable change instead of a timer, PAR sized from the\nmachine, the lane's build under the machine-wide lease, a retirement pass \u2014 and the lane's\n`MIPSTARRE_SKIP_HOOKS=1` fallback push deleted.\n\n**6. Self-repair janitor.** One idempotent sweep of five passes, each selecting by record\nfield: no date glob and no filename digit filter anywhere.\n\n**7. Merge hygiene and build reachability.** A committed `.gitattributes` union driver for the\nappend-only logs, asserted by `worktree-setup.sh`; and a reachability guard inside the\nexisting `local-ci/build` step that names a module left outside the umbrella import closure.\n\n**No proof-integrity mechanism is touched.** No change to `.githooks/*`,\n`merge_loss_guard.py`, `checked-push.sh`, the seven `pr_merge.py` gates, the eight canonical\n`local-ci/<step>` contexts or the review-verdict contract. The one place a current tool\n*bypassed* a gate \u2014 the lane's hook-skipping fallback push \u2014 is removed, which strengthens it.\n\n### Testing\n\nRun in the branch worktree on the build host.\n\n- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_*.py'` \u2192 **977 tests, OK**\n  (9 skipped: the historical useful-queue scenarios retired by #505). That is the command the\n  pre-commit hook runs, and it ran on every commit here that stages a `scripts/` file.\n- `bash -n` on all 24 changed shell files and both renderings of the generated PATH shim: clean.\n- `python3 -m py_compile` on all 26 changed Python files: clean. `json.load` on\n  `model-policy.json`, `capacity-pol\n\n---\nCloses #550\n",
